primitives.name: Damped Gaussian Random Walk
primitives.verbatim_quote: Skills dynamics: θ_t = β_t θ_{t-1} + u_t ε_t (damped Gaussian random walk; β_t=1 standard; ε_t may scale with elapsed days τ(t)-τ(t-1)).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'\\theta_t': 'team skill vector at time t (dimensionless)', '\\beta_t': 'damping factor (dimensionless)', 'u_t': 'random walk increment (dimensionless)', '\\varepsilon_t': 'noise scale (dimensionless)'}
primitives.assumptions: Skills evolve stochastically with constant damping and Gaussian noise.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When β_t → 0, skill becomes static; when β_t → 1, skill follows a random walk.

layer2.mapping: Models temporal evolution of team strength in GSE's dynamic rating system.
layer2.telemetry: Skill variance growth rate over time.

primitives.name: Skills-Outcomes Likelihood Model
primitives.verbatim_quote: Skills-outcome model: Pr{y_t|θ_t} = L(z_t/s; y_t), z_t = x_t^T θ_t = (home skills sum) - (away skills sum) with scheduling vectors x_t,h, x_t,a.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'y_t': 'observed outcome (binary/ternary)', 'z_t': 'difference in skill sums (dimensionless)', 's': 'scale parameter (dimensionless)', 'x_t': 'scheduling vector (team assignment)', '\\theta_t': 'skill vector (dimensionless)'}
primitives.assumptions: Outcome depends on skill difference with a known link function L.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When z_t approaches ±∞, outcome certainty increases.

layer2.mapping: Maps to Bradley-Terry, Davidson, and Thurston models via L(z/s; y).

primitives.name: Approximate Kalman Filtering
primitives.verbatim_quote: The recursion f(θ_t|y̲_t) ∝ Pr{y_t|θ_t} ∫ f(θ_t|θ_{t-1}) f(θ_{t-1}|y̲_{t-1}) dθ_{t-1} is made tractable by a Gaussian projection P[·] minimizing KL distance (Proposition 1), with three covariance models: full matrix (KF), diagonal/vector (vSKF), shared scalar (sSKF), plus fixed-variance fSKF and pure stochastic gradient SG.
primitives.assumptions: Posterior approximated by Gaussian distribution using KL minimization.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When likelihood is non-Gaussian, approximation error increases.

layer2.mapping: Enables efficient online inference in GSE's real-time rating engine.
layer2.telemetry: KL divergence between true and projected posteriors.

reasoning_traces.think:
The core innovation lies in deriving a universal Bayesian online rating framework through approximate Gaussian Kalman filtering. This allows systematic derivation of rating algorithms for any skills-outcome model and team size. The key insight is that the posterior belief update can be approximated via a Gaussian projection minimizing KL divergence. The skill dynamics follow a damped Gaussian random walk, capturing temporal evolution. Outcome likelihoods are modeled via link functions such as Bradley-Terry or Davidson, which map skill differences to probabilities. The resulting recursions—especially vSKF—are computationally efficient and suitable for real-time applications. The framework unifies Elo, Glicko, and TrueSkill under a common probabilistic structure, where each corresponds to different approximations of the same underlying belief propagation mechanism. Failure modes include poor model specification (e.g., using BT on Thurston data) or high noise levels, where simpler methods like SGD become competitive. The framework also supports handling home-field advantage via frequency-based estimation and provides uncertainty tracking essential for GSI’s conformal prediction layer.
